rules.name: Excessive bold emphasis
rules.description: Frequent bold fragments can turn prose into a sequence of labels.
rules.message: A single paragraph contains several bold fragments.
rules.suggestion: Keep emphasis for the one phrase readers must scan first.

rules.name: Title Case heading
rules.description: English prose headings usually read more naturally in sentence case.
rules.message: The heading capitalizes most content words.
rules.suggestion: Use sentence case unless a house style requires Title Case.

rules.name: Bold mini-heading list
rules.description: Lists with bold labels can fragment a connected argument into a template.
rules.message: The list item starts with a bold mini-heading.
rules.suggestion: Use a table, real headings, or connected prose depending on the information structure.

rules.name: Decorative emoji bullet
rules.description: Repeated emoji at list starts are decoration rather than information.
rules.message: An emoji is being used as a list bullet.
rules.suggestion: Keep emojis only where they carry meaning or match the author's established voice.

rules.name: List-dominated passage
rules.description: A high share of bullet lines can hide relationships that should be expressed in prose or a table.
rules.message: Most meaningful lines in this passage are list items.
rules.suggestion: Keep the list if items are independently scannable; otherwise restore the missing relationships.

rules.name: Dense em-dash usage
rules.description: Em dashes are valid punctuation; only unusual density is reported.
rules.message: Em dashes appear unusually often for the passage length.
rules.suggestion: Check whether commas, periods, parentheses, or fewer interruptions would read better.
